I need it. After last week's picks, I need to go into hiding. It was awful. When you can't get over .500 with the straight-up picks, you know it's a bad week. I went 6-8 straight up and 3-11 against the spread. I could flip a coin and do better. Maybe my cats will make my picks next week. My season records are now 54-38-1 straight up and 37-54-2 against the spread. That is vile. Time to turn it around, so I am going to the dogs. Let them bark. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET New England Patriots (+3) at Chicago Bears Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime This is a big game for both teams, a tough one for the road team on a short week. Both teams can score, which should make this a fun one to watch. I think the Patriots have the better defense and that will be the difference. They overcome the road to win a much-needed game. Pick: Patriots 28, Bears 27 Pittsburgh Steelers at New Orleans Saints (+3.5) Paris on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on NFL Network (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) These two are both coming off road victories and now have a long trip to play this one. The Steelers have been the more consistent team this year, but the Saints looked good last week against the Giants . This will be tight, but the Steelers take it. Pick: Steelers 27, Saints 26 San Francisco 49ers at Atlanta Falcons (+3.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The 49ers are rolling as the league's best team, especially on offense. But losing Mike Evans will hurt. The Falcons couldn't stop the Bears last week, so what's to think they will slow down Brock Purdy ? They might not. But the Falcons will keep up. It's close. Pick: 49ers 30, Falcons 28 Cleveland Browns at Tennessee Titans (+1.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Browns are 4-2 after beating Baltimore last week, while the Titans beat the Colts last week. Neither team is doing much on offense, which suggests this will be a low-scoring game. I think the Browns have a better defense, which will be the difference. They win it again on a late field goal. Pick: Browns 17, Titans 16 Indianapolis Colts (+6.5) at Minnesota Vikings The Vikings are off a bye, while the Colts are off a terrible home loss to the Titans. That led to the firing of general manager Chris Ballard. Maybe that gives the Colts a bump. Beating the Vikings' defense will mean a lot of Jonathan Taylor . I think we see that as the Colts keep it close, but just miss out on the upset. Pick: Vikings 21, Colts 18 Miami Dolphins (+4.5) at New York Jets The Dolphins are off their bye in search of their first victory, while the Jets lost to the Patriots last week. The Jets have the better team and their defense should be able to limit the Miami offense. But the Dolphins play hard and will also play well on defense. It's close. Pick: Jets 19, Dolphins 17 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+3.5) at Carolina Panthers The Bucs might have Baker Mayfield back for this one. That would be big. The Panthers are rolling on offense as Bryce Young is in the MVP conversation. It will stay that way, but the Bucs will hang around. Pick: Panthers 24, Bucs 23 Cincinnati Bengals (+3) at Baltimore Ravens The Bengals are coming off a bye, while the Ravens are coming off a loss to the Browns. They could have Lamar Jackson back from an ankle injury here, which certainly changes things. Even if he's back, I think Joe Burrow will have a big day throwing it. The improved Bengals defense will do the rest. Upset. Pick: Bengals 24, Ravens 23 New York Giants (+10) at Houston Texans Who starts at quarterback for the Giants? It should be J.J. McCarthy , but we will see. No matter who starts, the Texans ' defense is having issues. The Giants will move the ball. But they won't stop C.J. Stroud . He's on fire and that gets the Texans the victory. Pick: Texans 27, Giants 23 Denver Broncos at Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Cardinals are coming off a big road upset of the Rams , while Denver beat Seattle last Thursday. The Denver offense has been lifeless so far this season. But the defense is still sticky. I think that defense will come up big, while Bo Nix finally makes some plays. It's close. Pick: Broncos 24, Cardinals 21 Green Bay Packers (+3) at Detroit Lions Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Lions are coming off a bye, which they needed, while the Packers are coming off consecutive victories. They are playing much better on both sides of the ball. The two defenses will be challenged here, but the Lions will be the better offense at home coming off the bye. Lions win it by a tiny margin as both quarterbacks light it up. Pick: Lions 34, Packers 33 Los Angeles Rams at Las Vegas Raiders (+4.5) This is a must-win for both teams, as they are on losing streaks. The Rams have a lot of injury issues, which have really impacted their team. They still have Matt Stafford. He can light up a defense, which he will do here. But the Rams will give up some big plays to the Raiders , who hang around. Pick: Rams 28, Raiders 27 Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) at Seattle Seahawks Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a revenge game for Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker , who was the Super Bowl MVP for Seattle last February. And let's not forget the Chiefs have Patrick Mahomes . Seattle is good on defense, but their offense is turning the ball over. That matters here. Chiefs take it. Pick: Chiefs 23, Seahawks 17 Dallas Cowboys at Philadelphia Eagles (+4.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Eagles are a mess with all the injuries, including quarterback Jalen Hurts being out for the year. The Cowboys have struggled on offense the past two weeks, which isn't a good look. This is desperation time for these two. The Cowboys will win it, but it's close. Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel gave the Bears defense plenty of credit. The matchup of 4-2 teams in primetime will certainly gave some haymakers thrown from each side. away.blurb: The New England Patriots will likely roll out a shorthanded squad on Thursday for their primetime matchup against the Bears at Soldier Field. Speaking after Sunday's win, Coach Mike Vrabel was candid about the availability of his banged-up players, especially in an abbreviated week with little downtime available. "It's a short week," Vrabel said. "So whether they can make it back or not, I don't know. They don't finish the game. We'll have to see. But I don't know [anything] other than that. And we'll just have to figure out who we have available and find 48 [players] to put out there. So it's just hard to say, but it's a short week. And if you don't finish the game, that's a quick turnaround." It was just a walkthrough, but Moses' "limited" status at least offers some sliver of hope that the veteran tackle could be back on the gridiron for Thursday's game against the Bears. As for the latest limited returnee to New England's secondary, Davis had been downgraded before the Pittsburgh Steelers matchup in September because of a neck issue. He then stayed sidelined for consecutive weeks of practice while a pair of rookie corners both missed autumn action with hamstring ailments. Against Tampa Bay he went 4-for-5, with makes from 52 and 58 yards. That was his second straight game with multiple field goals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) New Orleans allows 29.7 points and 377.7 yards per game. Those numbers suggest Pittsburgh will move the ball. Some of those drives will stall before the end zone, and that is where Boswell scores. The prediction goes beyond another solid outing. Boswell makes five field goals, including two from beyond 50 yards. The limitation is his four misses this season, which show he is not automatic from long range. Tyler Shough throws two interceptions Shough has a 12:5 touchdown-to-interception ratio through six games. He threw only 144 yards against the Giants, though he scored four touchdowns in total. He is also playing through broken bones in his non-throwing hand, which may explain why he has just 242 passing yards over the last two weeks. Predicting two interceptions means Shough nearly matches his early-season total in one afternoon. The route to that outcome is straightforward. Pittsburgh's lead will push New Orleans into longer passing situations, and an injured hand makes tight-window throws harder. The call is that one pass is tipped and picked off in the second half, while another is forced into coverage on a late drive. Those turnovers would turn a competitive game into a Steelers cushion. There is a counterpoint. Shough has produced touchdowns despite modest yardage, so this prediction depends on game script more than on his recent efficiency. Chris Olave posts 120 yards and two touchdowns in a losing rally Olave had double-digit targets in each of the first four games. Over the last two he has seen only 13 targets, producing an 8-89-1 line. That drop in volume looks like the sort of dip that corrects itself. Pittsburgh's defense will give him room to correct it. New Orleans' opponents have averaged 256.0 passing yards per game, which suggests quarterbacks can find openings in this matchup. Rookie Germie Bernard's 11-catch, 87-yard, one-touchdown game against the Steelers' last opponent shows how that kind of volume can arise. Olave reaches 10 targets, 120 yards and two touchdowns as New Orleans chases points. Those scores help the Saints cut a two-score deficit to three points late in the fourth quarter. Pittsburgh still holds on. The prediction is Steelers 31, Saints 27, with Boswell's late field goal sealing it. If Jordyn Tyson makes his debut after traveling with the team while recovering from a hamstring injury, the Saints' receiving group could be even more dangerous. These are deliberately high-variance predictions, not the most likely outcomes. The underlying numbers favor Pittsburgh, but turnovers and a motivated passing offense can make this matchup less predictable than the records suggest. Buccaneers vs. Steelers: Final injury report for Week 6
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and several key players will be unavailable as Tampa Bay looks to build on last week's victory over Dallas. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) has officially been ruled out after missing all three practices this week. Rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start after leading the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season last Thursday against the Cowboys. The Buccaneers will also be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), who did not participate in practice throughout the week. Wide receiver David Sills V (hamstring) was also ruled out despite being listed as a full participant in all three practices. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is listed as doubtful, while linebackers SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and Josiah Trotter (knee), cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle), and running back Sean Tucker (quad) are questionable. Dennis and Garnes were full participants Friday, providing some encouraging news heading into the weekend. Pittsburgh is also dealing with several injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out, along with safety DeShon Elliott (knee). Wide receiver DK Metcalf was added to Friday's report with an illness and is questionable. The 49ers’ possibility of signing Joey carries more than just professional significance. It also carries a personal touch: the brothers haven’t played together since their high school days. That was in 2012. Their mother, Cheryl Bosa, really hopes to see Joey in a San Francisco 49ers jersey, just like her other son, Nick. Joey is a former Los Angeles Chargers edge defender who represented the Buffalo Bills in 2025. He recorded 5.0 sacks, 5 forced fumbles, 16 quarterback hits, and 9 tackles for loss in 15 games during the 2025 season. He had signed a one-year, $12M contract with the Bills in March 2025. There was no renewal. He didn’t consider a comeback in the 2026 offseason. Nick said that Joey’s more into golf than the NFL. But there was no retirement news either. This leaves the NFL comeback speculation alive and well and doing cyberspace rounds. He was a capable threat in Buffalo last season, and his extensive experience and pass-rushing ability could make him a useful rotational defender if he ever returns to a team that also features his younger brother, Nick. Joey Bosa retirement rumors continue despite NFL interest Across 10 seasons with the Los Angeles Chargers and Buffalo Bills, he recorded 77 sacks and 22 forced fumbles in 122 games. If he could win a Super Bowl alongside his younger brother Nick Bosa, wouldn’t that be the best closing chapter to his NFL career? We can only hope for that to happen. Or maybe he has retired. The move that grabbed the most attention this week was probably the signing of quarterback Andy Dalton and the release of quarterback Cooper Rush. But the Falcons will probably get more help on the field from their defensive signings. They signed edge rusher Charles Snowden off of the Commanders' practice squad yesterday, and later they announced they added rookie linebacker TJ Quinn to the practice squad. Quinn is a native of Valdosta, Ga. and went to Lowndes High School. He spent four years at Louisville and had an extremely productive career. In 2025, he posted 95 tackles with 8 tackles for loss, 3 sacks, and 2 interceptions. He had 82 tackles as a junior and 92 tackles as a sophomore. He signed with the Green Bay Packers as an undrafted free agent, but didn't make the initial 53-man roster. At 6'0 and 225 pounds, Quinn had a good Pro Day with the Cardinals in the fall, clocking a 4.53 forty, but it wasn't enough to get him drafted. Deablo is the veteran, and he's had a relatively poor season. He missed some time in training camp with an ankle injury, and he's looked a step slow laterally. He's on the final year of a two-year deal, and at this rate, the Falcons likely wouldn't bring him back next season, preferring to hand the reins full-time to Daniels and Perkins. The Falcons' linebackers have a tough matchup this week as they are understaffed with the San Francisco 49ers coming to Mercedes-Benz. Running back Christian McCaffrey, tight end George Kittle, and wide receiver Deebo Samuel are all players who will stress the second level of the defense. Kickoff is at 1 p,m. EST on FOX. picks.blurb: Why the Titans Will Beat the Browns in Week 7, Why They Won't, and a Prediction Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code DraftKings Promo Code FanDuel Promo Code Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code DraftKings Predictions Promo Novig Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI I'm all about celebrating a win, but the Tennessee Titans are coming up on a must-win game against the Cleveland Browns in Week 7. Can a previously 0-5 squad keep pushing the turnaround and secure their second straight victory? Last week's win over the Indianapolis Colts represented a new wave of promise for the Titans. But in the Browns, Tennessee will face the top team (in a three-way tie) in the AFC North. Cleveland has come on strong, and are coming to Nashville off a 13-10 win over the Baltimore Ravens. In the wake of a long-awaited win, I've got one reason the Titans will beat the Browns, one reason they won't, as well as my own prediction. Will: Robert Saleh's defense takes over again Robert Saleh's defense just had their best performance of the season. Almost single-handedly, the score-stopping unit bottled up the Colts' offense when it mattered. The Titans forced multiple turnovers and forced Daniel Jones to make mistakes through the air. If Tennessee finds a way to win again this week, it will likely be due to a similar performance from the defense. Expect Saleh to send the heat once again after last week's six-sack outing. PFF has the Browns' offensive line ranked all the way down at 26th in the NFL. If the Titans' defensive line can force Deshaun Watson to unsettle in the pocket, we could be in for a similar path to victory for Tennessee. Won't: Browns get young playmakers going Oppositely, with the Titans' offense still operating at an inconsistent level, this game could get out of hand if Cleveland gets their young playmakers going. Oct 11, 2026; East Rutherford, New Jersey, USA; Cleveland Browns wide receiver Denzel Boston (12) scores on a touchdown reception during the fourth quarter against New York Jets cornerback Brandon Stephens (21) at MetLife Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Robert Deutsch-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Guys like Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in the Browns' WR core are the sort that can change a game, and fast. Harold Fannin is one of the best rising TEs in the league, too; Cleveland has options, and offensive-minded head coach Todd Monken has led them to a surprising 4-2 tally as a result. Guys like Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion in the Browns' WR core are the sort that can change a game, and fast. Harold Fannin is one of the best rising TEs in the league, too; Cleveland has options, and offensive-minded head coach Todd Monken has led them to a surprising 4-2 tally as a result. Tennessee's defense needs to set the tone early. If the Browns come out swinging, and the Titans' offense takes as long as usual to get into any kind of rhythm, the team could be facing another steep halftime deficit. I just don't like their odds to overcome that two weeks in a row, even if this game is in Nashville. Prediction: Titans win, 17-14 However, I don't believe the Titans will have to worry about that. I'll err to to the positive side with my prediction (something I could be accused of doing too often) and say that Saleh's defense has another big game on the way to a Titans win. This team hasn't won two straight games since Weeks 10 and 11 of the 2022 season. That's a vile streak, but after last week's victory, now feels like the perfect time for Tennessee to break it. Saleh finally has his legs under him as a head coach with this team. The Browns haven't scored more than 13 points in two weeks. In front of a potentially revamped home crowd, the stars are aligning for a home upset for Tennessee. I don't believe the offense will take any major strides, but in Week 7, maybe they won't have to. I predict a narrow Titans win over the Browns. Published 2 hours ago LANE MILLS Lane covers the Tennessee Titans, where he brings an evolving team's journey to fans on a daily basis. picks.headline: Titans scouting report vs Cleveland Browns, matchups, prediction NFL Week 7
picks.blurb: News Sports Counties Business Real Estate Advertise Obituaries eNewspaper Legals TITANS Titans scouting report vs Cleveland Browns, matchups, prediction NFL Week 7 Tyler Palmateer Nashville Tennessean Oct. 21, 2026, 5:07 a.m. CT The Tennessee Titans are seeking their first consecutive win since 2022 after a victory over the Indianapolis Colts. Tennessee's offense ranks last in the NFL in yards per game, and quarterback Cam Ward had career lows in his last outing. Can the Tennessee Titans win twice in a row? That’s no small feat for an organization that hasn’t won consecutive games since 2022. But Tennessee’s 26-20 win over the Indianapolis Colts in NFL Week 6 quieted the storm after an 0-5 start. Now, the Titans (1-5) can prove it wasn’t a fluke when it hosts the Cleveland Browns (4-2) at Nissan Stadium on Oct. 25 (noon CT, CBS). The Browns are 1.5-point favorites. They lost last year's meeting 31-29 after Tennessee running back Tony Pollard rushed for a career-high 161 yards and two touchdowns. Questions remain for quarterback Cam Ward and the Titans' offense, who were bailed out by the defense and special teams against the Colts . Ward’s 11 completions and 102 yards passing against the Colts were career lows, and Tennessee still ranks last in the NFL in yards per game (236.3) and tied for last in points per game (14.0). Here’s our scouting report for the Titans’ game against the Browns. One Cleveland Browns stat to know Other than the Baltimore Ravens ’ opening touchdown drive last week, the Browns surrendered three points and 169 yards of total offense to finish a 13-10 victory. Cleveland hasn’t been atop the AFC North this late in the season since 2014. Where Tennessee Titans have edge vs. Browns Tennessee spent offseason resources beefing up its pass rush for coach Robert Saleh’s defensive scheme. The results finally surfaced with six sacks and 25 pressures against the Colts. Doing that again could hamper quarterback Deshaun Watson and the Browns, who have surrendered a league-high 24 sacks in six games. Cleveland left tackle Spencer Fano and right guard Austin Barber are both rookies. Titans eighth-year veteran Jeffery Simmons is arguably the NFL’s best defensive tackle. He has a team-high four sacks and 26 hurries. Where Cleveland Browns have edge vs. Titans Tennessee’s passing offense is the NFL’s worst at 153.5 yards per game, and the Browns rank eighth in passing defense at 205.2 yards per game. Pro Bowl cornerback Denzel Ward anchors a Cleveland secondary that ranks sixth in coverage grade at 71.1, according to Pro Football Focus. Cornerback Myles Harden has five passes defended this season. The Titans likely won’t win another game with a blocked punt return and four second-half field goals like they did against the Colts. If the Browns limit Cam Ward’s explosive plays downfield — they had six pass breakups against the Ravens — then Tennessee will struggle to score. Cam Ward has developed a go-to target in rookie receiver Carnell Tate, which is good. But receivers beyond Tate (44 targets) and Wan’Dale Robinson (37) aren’t that involved. Running back Tyjae Spears has more targets (17) than receiver Calvin Ridley (five). Elic Ayomanor has shown flashes of playmaking, but he’s averaging two targets the past four games and had a bad drop against the Colts. Score prediction: Browns 21, Titans 10 Ward’s limitations are clear through six games, giving Cleveland’s secondary a near-perfect blueprint. If nothing pops for Tennessee’s offense, the scoring woes will continue. Tyler Palmateer covers the Tennessee Titans for The Tennessean. Have a story idea for Tyler? We still don’t even know if Lamar Jackson is playing in this game and we certainly know that there are plenty of Browns that are still idle, still ailing and not sure they’re going to play.” Still, there’s reason to think at least some of those names could return by Sunday. Schwesinger finished last week’s Jets game. Labbe noted that Schwesinger and Graham are “two guys that wouldn’t shock me if we walked out there (Friday) morning and they’re both in the stretch lines getting ready to go.” CLEVELAND, Ohio — 38 players. Two injury reports. Zero certainty about who will actually suit up Sunday when the Browns host the Ravens at Huntington Bank Field with first place in the AFC North on the line. That’s the impossible situation both teams — and anyone trying to analyze this game — find themselves in heading into one of the biggest divisional matchups of the young NFL season. The Browns’ injury list includes defensive cornerstones Carson Schwesinger, Mason Graham and Mike Hall — none of whom had practiced through Thursday. For a defense that’s been Cleveland’s identity all season, those aren’t small absences. Browns beat reporter Ashley Bastock zeroed in on what the late-week practice absences actually mean in practical terms. “It’s always a little concerning when you get to Thursday and they haven’t been on the practice field at all because that does become a really tight turnaround,” she said. “And I think ultimately it’s why we’re going into picking this game, really just having no clue what to do or what’s going to decide it, because it’s really hard to know those things when you don’t know who’s actually going to be on the field.” The Browns have shown real depth this season. Backup defenders Adin Huntington and Sam Kamara performed well against the Jets even without a full complement of starters. But there’s a ceiling to how much depth can compensate. As Labbe put it: “Your starters and your stars are starters and stars for a reason. And eventually, if you don’t have those guys, that can catch up to you.” The Ravens face their own uncertainty — a reshuffled offensive line, Flowers’ toe injury and a quarterback who hasn’t practiced all week. Friday’s practice will be the key for both rosters. Whatever happens, Sunday’s game may ultimately be decided less by scheme than by which injury report clears up first. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit cleveland.com. away.headline: Denzel Boston limited at Cleveland Browns practice with injury
away.blurb: The 6-foot-4 pass catcher was still able to practice in a limited capacity, which is a good sign for his availability on Sunday when the Browns take on the Baltimore Ravens. The second-round pick in April's draft leads the NFL with 20.6 yards per reception, while his 330 yards and 3 touchdowns are the best among all rookies. Boston has tallied 16 catches through the first five games of the year and has been a big part of the Browns starting the season at 3-2, which has them tied for second place in the AFC North. However, after pulling in 3 catches for 46 yards and a touchdown against the New York Jets, Boston popped up on Cleveland's injury report on Wednesday with a foot issue. Throughout the year, Boston has made an early impression on the NFL, displaying why he was such a key piece of Jedd Fisch's offense in the head coach's first two seasons on Montlake. "Not making things too big, just keeping the main thing the main thing," Boston said of his poise and early success . "And also just understanding the camaraderie that we built around the building, having the trust that he's going to go make that play or he's going to go make that play. I think it just comes from a great locker room, a brotherhood, and an understanding of everyone's here for their purpose and everyone's going to fulfill their purpose when the time comes." Trey Hendrickson Will Make His Return "We're always going to try to have the best interest of the player," Minter said. "The path that we went down was really in [Hendrickson]'s best interest, both short-term and long-term. [I'm] excited for him to be back out there." The Ravens ruled out defensive tackle Broderick Washington Jr. (ankle), who didn't practice Thursday or Friday. He has six tackles so far this season. Lane had three full days of practice this week and is listed as questionable. He would have to be removed from injured reserve this weekend to play. It seems like every week a big favorite is being upset, and Week 6 had two of them as the Los Angeles Rams (12.5-point favorites) lost outright at home to the Arizona Cardinals while the Indianapolis Colts (seven-point favorites) lost an AFC South battle with the previously winless Tennessee Titans. So, if you’re still alive in Survivor heading into Week 7, you deserve a ton of credit. The SI Betting team was banged up in Week 6, as managing editor Peter Dewey came up short with his Colts pick. On the bright side, those of our readers that tailed senior editor Iain MacMlllam, the New England Patriots improved to 19-2 in their last 21 home games against the New York Jets with a victory on Sunday. The Patriots have won three games in a row and are suddenly back in the mix to earn the top seed in the AFC this season. Week 7 doesn’t feature a ton of obvious Survivor spots, as the Houston Texans (9.5-point favorites against the New York Giants), Minnesota Vikings (5.5-point favorites against the Colts) and Rams (5.5-point favorites against the Las Vegas Raiders) are the three teams favored by the most on Sunday. So, Survivor players are going to have to at least consider a closer game to keep themselves alive. Here’s a quick recap of the Week 6 picks before we share our Week 7 selections. NFL Week 6 Survivor Picks Recap Peter Dewey: Indianapolis Colts (L) Iain MacMillan: New England Patriots (W) It wasn’t a perfect week in these picks, but as always we’ll allow Dewey to “buy back in” so we can share differing perspectives each week in these picks. Week 7 may be the toughest week of the season, as some quality teams (Buffalo, Jacksonville mainly) are on the bye. Washington and the Los Angeles Chargers also won’t play in Week 7. Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook NFL Week 7 Survivor Pool Picks New York Jets Geno Smith and the New York Jets are off to a 2-4 start, but they’ve been competent so far this season. Not only are the Jets 4-1-1 against the spread, but they rank sixth in the NFL in opponent yards per play and are 10th in EPA/Play on defense. The offense isn’t nearly as good (19th in EPA/Play, 22nd in yards per play), but the Jets have a very favorable matchup against a winless Miami Dolphins team – at home – in Week 7. Miami is coming off a bye, but it has just one game all season where it’s scored more than 13 points. The Dolphins rank 28th in EPA/Play, 27th in success rate and 22nd in yards per play allowed through five games this season. While I don’t believe either one of these squads is a playoff team, the Jets have a much higher floor with Geno Smith under center. New York has also hung around with playoff contenders like Green Bay, Detroit and New England while beating a 4-2 Cleveland team in Week 5. I have no faith in this Miami team, which seems destined for a top-three pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. Miami had a backdoor cover against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 5, but it has relied on garbage time to get back into games that never were really close to begin with. With De’Von Achane out for the season, Malik Willis doesn’t have enough help to really get this offense going, and now he has to take on a Jets unit that has been one of the better ones in the NFL. Since the Texans are the only big favorite on the board this week – and they're just 2-4 themselves in 2026 – I don’t mind taking a shot on the Jets. I can’t imagine another spot (outside of their road game vs. Miami) where I’d really feel comfortable taking them in Survivor. – Peter Dewey Minnesota Vikings Despite the Minnesota Vikings being undefeated so far this season, this might be the last week I'd feel confident taking them. They're fresh off a bye week and have arguably the best defense in the NFL. That very same defense is going to be able to put Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis Colts' offense in a blender. It's clear by now that the key to beating the Colts is stopping Jonathan Taylor, and the Vikings rank in the top three in virtually every single run defense stat. It was the first victory of the season for the Titans, and the Colts couldn’t get out of their own way all afternoon. They turned the ball over three times, including a pair of interceptions from Daniel Jones, and also had a punt that was blocked by the Titans and returned for a touchdown. away.blurb: Green Bay has a more immediate reason to consider the idea. Defensive tackle Javon Hargrave is out for the season with an Achilles injury. The Packers also placed Jonathan Ford on injured reserve before their Week 6 victory over the Dallas Cowboys . The possibility of Buckner becoming available following Ballard’s firing has already generated speculation, although the Colts haven’t announced any plans to trade him. The Green Bay Packers have already lost one veteran defensive tackle for the season. Now, a new trade proposal has them looking to the Indianapolis Colts for another established player who could help their defense down the stretch. DeForest Buckner has continued to produce in Indianapolis, but the Colts are 2-4, general manager Chris Ballard has been fired and the 32-year-old made his frustration clear following Sunday’s loss to the Tennessee Titans. With the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline approaching, Green Bay has been named as a potential landing spot for Buckner in a deal that wouldn’t require a premium draft pick. DeForest Buckner Trade Pitch Names Packers as Suitor Bleacher Report’s Kristopher Knox listed Buckner at No. 4 on his Oct. 21 trade block rankings, projecting a 2027 fourth-round pick as the price to acquire him. Knox named the Packers and San Francisco 49ers as potential suitors. The proposal followed the Colts’ decision to fire Ballard on Monday, one day after a 26-20 home loss to the previously winless Titans. Indianapolis named assistant GM Ed Dodds to oversee its personnel department for the remainder of the season. Knox suggested the leadership change could put veteran players on the market if ownership decides to shift its focus toward the future. “Premier defensive tackles generally command strong returns, and Buckner is still one of those, even at 32,” Knox wrote. Buckner has started all six games this season, totaling 26 tackles, four sacks and three passes defended. The three-time Pro Bowler is in the final year of his contract, which could make him a short-term addition for a team pursuing a playoff run. His comments following the loss to Tennessee have also attracted attention. “I’m sick and tired of the same song and dance every year,” Buckner said, via NFL.com’s Kevin Patra . Buckner also said he still had confidence in the people in Indianapolis when asked about the coaching staff and front office. His comments were about the Colts’ struggles, rather than a trade request. DeForest Buckner Could Address Packers’ Injury-Hit Defense The team signed former first-round pick Mazi Smith to its practice squad Tuesday, but that move provides depth rather than the proven interior pass rush Buckner could offer alongside Devonte Wyatt. The Packers are 4-2 following their 23-13 win over Dallas, their third straight victory. Their defense intercepted Dak Prescott twice and held the Cowboys to 48 rushing yards. Some change has already happened, with general manager Chris Ballard getting fired Monday morning. But he might not be the only one on the move this season. It might be a sell-off this year, even though they don't have their own first-round pick. The reason for that? The Sauce Gardner trade. That, too, has taken a bad turn, unfortunately due to an injury. According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Gardner has a calf strain and is going to miss some time for the Colts. Indianapolis is going to be without their top cornerback going forward, as a challenged defense is going to be in a bit more trouble. Sauce Gardner has a calf strain, likely to miss time for Colts "More Colts news: Pro Bowl CB Sauce Gardner, who was unable to finish Sunday's loss to the Titans , has a mild calf strain that makes him week-to-week, sources say after the MRI," Rapoport reports. This update for the Colts' top cornerback is a massively unfortunate one. This mild calf strain is not season-ending, and it might not be an IR stint either. But, as Rapoport notes, Gardner is "expected to miss some time" as he recovers from this calf strain. Fortunately, it's not a lengthy injury. But the timing of the injury is really bad news for the Colts. MORE : Colts fans are calling for Daniel Jones benching after ugly Titans loss Coming off a loss to the Titans, who came into the matchup at 0-5, the now 2-4 Colts are tied with the Houston Texans in the AFC South and face an uphill battle to make the playoffs. Add in that Daniel Jones hasn't looked as good as he did last season, the Colts just fired their general manager, and there's plenty of instability with this team coming off a loss to the Titans. Now, Gardner's hurt and will miss some time. Indianapolis is heading into Week 7 against the Minnesota Vikings , who are set to be without their top cornerback, which might lead Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison to have big days against an already leaky Colts' secondary. home.blurb: The Minnesota Vikings were enjoying their bye week undefeated , but they'll be back in action in Week 7 against the Indianapolis Colts. Ahead of the game, they've received some good news surrounding their running back room, as Jordan Mason is set to return to the field, according to Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. "Vikings RB Jordan Mason has been designated for return. His practice window opens, though he's still on IR," Rapoport wrote on X, formerly Twitter. Mason suffered a hand injury in Week 1 that forced him to go on injured reserve, and it's good news that he's been able to progress at the right time to return. It looks like he could be back in the coming weeks, if not against the Colts, and that should be no problem, as Aaron Jones Sr. has led the backfield. Jordan Mason's return from a broken thumb, which should happen in Week 7, won't create big headlines, but it's important for the Vikings. Aaron Jones, Sr., filled in well, but he's 31 years old, and asking him to handle almost all of the running back duties was not a long-term plan. Mason and Jones form a good committee, and they can resume their roles. The Vikings face the reeling Colts this weekend before a four-game stretch that will define their season: at Lions, vs. Bills, at Packers, vs. 49ers (in Mexico City). Wes Phillips on Jordan Mason's Return to Practice, Kyler Murray, & Collaboration Among Coaching Staff NFL Power Rankings: Vikings Status After Week 6 Bye Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS While the Minnesota Vikings took a breath during their Week 6 bye, the northern footprint of professional football continued its strong start to 2026. The four NFC North and four AFC North teams are all above .500 entering Week 7. Of the 24 franchises residing outside the two divisions, only eight currently hold a record above .500. In the NFC North specifically, non-divisional opponents are being dispatched at an astonishing 13-3 clip (.813), with the AFC North right behind in the same category at 12-5 (.706). This puts the "Black and Blue Division" on pace to match a level of divisional dominance seen only twice since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger, per NFL Media Research. The other two instances? You guessed it: the 2023 AFC North and last year's NFC North, when all four teams in those divisions finished those campaigns with winning records. Despite not playing a single snap this past weekend, Minnesota was able to climb the ladder in this week's power rankings, with its biggest jump being six spots. Here's a look at where the Vikings landed heading into Week 7: No. 4 (up 3 spots): Nick Shook – NFL.com No. 3 (no change): Gary Davenport – Bleacher Report There isn't a more surprising team in the NFL this year (at least in a positive way) than the undefeated Minnesota Vikings. Naysayers will point to a relatively easy schedule and offensive inconsistency as reasons why they aren't as good their record. But Minnesota's ultra-aggressive defense is legit: second in yards allowed, third against the pass, fifth against the run and first in points allowed.

away.headline: Dolphins-Jets Injury Update: Bye Leaves Key Miami Questions Open
away.blurb: Miami's Week 6 bye prevents the Dolphins from issuing a conventional Friday game-status report, so no player should be labeled officially out or questionable for the Oct. 25 Jets game unless the club has made that designation. The week still produced several important health developments. Right guard Jonah Savaiinaea did not participate in Tuesday's voluntary practice after leaving the Cincinnati game with an ankle injury. Linebacker Jordyn Brooks, edge rusher Robert Beal Jr., cornerback Reese Taylor, running back Jaylen Wright and receiver Caleb Douglas also sat out. Because it was a bye-week session, some absences may have been precautionary. The Jets' Friday report belongs to their Week 6 game, not the Miami matchup. Breece Hall, guard Dylan Parham, receiver Adonai Mitchell and edge rusher Joseph Ossai were listed out after missing practice with injuries. Safety Dane Belton and tight end Kenyon Sadiq carried questions, while Omar Cooper Jr. entered a return window from injured reserve. Whatever happens in New York's game this weekend will become the starting point for its Miami report. The matchup implications are significant. If Savaiinaea cannot return, Jarrett Kingston is the likely replacement against a Jets defense with 17 sacks. If Brents, Taylor or Duck remain unavailable, Miami will again ask young defensive backs to cover Garrett Wilson. If Hall's quadriceps injury lingers, Braelon Allen would become New York's primary runner. Cornerbacks Storm Duck and Darrell Baker Jr., edge defender Trey Moore and other eligible players may become options when game-week practice begins. De'Von Achane remains on injured reserve with a knee injury and is not expected to play against New York. Gordon therefore remains the lead back, with Wright and Kaytron Allen behind him if healthy. The first official Dolphins-Jets injury report is expected next Wednesday. Until then, this is a watch list, not a final designation sheet.

With the bye week over for the Miami Dolphins, the team is now gearing up to take on the New York Jets on Sunday. Bye weeks are usually a good time for injured players to get an extra week of recovery before coming back, and that could be the case for multiple key players. Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley offered some injury updates on those key players, including wide receiver Caleb Douglas and right guard Jonah Savaiinaea. Additionally, on offense is guard Savaiinaea. He suffered an ankle injury in Week 5 and missed the second half of the game. Running back Jaylen Wright also had a reaggravation of his foot injury, but Hafley stated that the back may be ready to go on Wednesday. home.headline: Dolphins-Jets Injury Update: Bye Leaves Key Miami Questions Open
home.blurb: Miami's Week 6 bye prevents the Dolphins from issuing a conventional Friday game-status report, so no player should be labeled officially out or questionable for the Oct. 25 Jets game unless the club has made that designation. The week still produced several important health developments. Right guard Jonah Savaiinaea did not participate in Tuesday's voluntary practice after leaving the Cincinnati game with an ankle injury. Linebacker Jordyn Brooks, edge rusher Robert Beal Jr., cornerback Reese Taylor, running back Jaylen Wright and receiver Caleb Douglas also sat out. Because it was a bye-week session, some absences may have been precautionary. The Jets' Friday report belongs to their Week 6 game, not the Miami matchup. Breece Hall, guard Dylan Parham, receiver Adonai Mitchell and edge rusher Joseph Ossai were listed out after missing practice with injuries. Safety Dane Belton and tight end Kenyon Sadiq carried questions, while Omar Cooper Jr. entered a return window from injured reserve. Whatever happens in New York's game this weekend will become the starting point for its Miami report. The matchup implications are significant. If Savaiinaea cannot return, Jarrett Kingston is the likely replacement against a Jets defense with 17 sacks. If Brents, Taylor or Duck remain unavailable, Miami will again ask young defensive backs to cover Garrett Wilson. If Hall's quadriceps injury lingers, Braelon Allen would become New York's primary runner. home.headline: New York Jets receive mixed bag of news on injury report ahead of crucial AFC East showdown against New England Patriots
home.blurb: The Jets will be without two important offensive playmakers against New England, but the return of a promising young rookie provides some much-needed optimism. Let's start with the bad. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that two key weapons on the offense, in both running back Breece Hall, who has a quad injury, and wide receiver AD Mitchell, who has a finger injury, have been ruled out for Sunday's game against New England. That's not how it played out. Hall sat out against Chicago, missed last week's win over the Cleveland Browns , and now he's going to miss a third straight game. Look, at this point, the Jets could have put him on IR and freed up a roster spot. They haven't done that, and for whatever reason, the team keeps holding the door open for a return that hasn't come. That's been frustrating to watch. I'm high on both of these guys. Cooper gives the Jets a receiver who can take attention away from Wilson on the outside, and Sadiq is a matchup problem for linebackers and safeties. With Hall and Mitchell out, the Jets need their young talent to step up, and this is the perfect spot for both rookies to show what they can do. Breece Hall's absence is getting frustrating Hall suffered his quad injury in Week 3 against the Detroit Lions , and the Jets labeled him “week to week” for the injury report. Now, I know only a few weeks have passed since that game. But when I heard week to week, I figured Hall would miss Week 4 against the Chicago Bears and that might be it. Losing Mitchell on top of Hall stings, too. Outside of Garrett Wilson, Mitchell has been one of the few perimeter options this offense can lean on, and his finger injury takes another piece off the board. We haven't really gotten to see him in a Jets uniform making plays yet. He made one play against the Titans and got hurt on it. home.headline: Breece Hall Injury Update: When Is NY Jets RB Coming Back?
home.blurb: According to a Tuesday post from NBC Sports, Breece Hall suffered a quadriceps injury in New York's 31-24 loss to the Detroit Lions. The injury has kept him out of the lineup since. He missed Week 5's contest against the Cleveland Browns due to the injury. According to Jets head coach Aaron Glenn, Breece Hall was ruled out for Week 5 on Friday. It took the week to arrive at the decision, which may have indicated that he might be close to returning. However, this does not guarantee he will be available in Week 6. Glenn called Hall week-to-week before he ruled him out, which hinted that he could still miss time. If he upgrades the estimate to day-to-day, that would give him a much better chance of playing. For now, managers should operate as if he's not playing and look elsewhere until a more emphatic, positive update is available. At this time of the season, the running back options on the waiver wire are scarce. One option that might be available in some leagues is Jets backup running back Braelon Allen. Allen rushed 38 times for 175 yards on the ground in his last two games. If you have access to him, it would be a simple switch. Once Hall is cleared for action, you can start Hall. A deep one-week solution that could get some production is the Bills' backup running back Ty Johnson. Johnson earned four catches for 72 yards against the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football. It was his second game in three weeks in which he earned at least 50 receiving yards. If you are in a PPR league, Johnson could be a one-week start that could buy time for Hall to return. Tyler Allgeier could be one waiver wire option worth checking out. Allgeier scored a touchdown in Week 4 against the New York Giants. If anything happens to Jeremiyah Love, who has already visited the injury report this season, Allgeier will be in line for a noticeable number of carries. Even if Hall returns, it might be worth stashing Allgeier beyond a one-week substitute role. When Will Myles Garrett Be Back? away.headline: Buccaneers vs. Steelers: Final injury report for Week 6
away.blurb: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have released their final injury report ahead of Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers, and several key players will be unavailable as Tampa Bay looks to build on last week's victory over Dallas. Quarterback Baker Mayfield (right thumb) has officially been ruled out after missing all three practices this week. Rookie Jalon Daniels will make his third consecutive start after leading the Buccaneers to their first victory of the season last Thursday against the Cowboys. The Buccaneers will also be without safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (rib), who did not participate in practice throughout the week. Wide receiver David Sills V (hamstring) was also ruled out despite being listed as a full participant in all three practices. Cornerback Benjamin Morrison (quad) is listed as doubtful, while linebackers SirVocea Dennis (ankle/foot) and Josiah Trotter (knee), cornerback Ayden Garnes (ankle), and running back Sean Tucker (quad) are questionable. Dennis and Garnes were full participants Friday, providing some encouraging news heading into the weekend. Pittsburgh is also dealing with several injuries, particularly at wide receiver. Roman Wilson (finger) and Ben Skowronek (calf) have been ruled out, along with safety DeShon Elliott (knee). Wide receiver DK Metcalf was added to Friday's report with an illness and is questionable. away.headline: Steelers at Tampa Bay Buccaneers Gameday: Injury Updates, Depth Charts, TV Info, Betting Lines, More
away.blurb: Three Pittsburgh Steelers have been ruled out for the team's Week 6 game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday, and five more are questionable to suit up, according to the team's Friday injury report. Two wide receivers Ben Skowronek and Roman Wilson left the team's 34-22 Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts with injures and did not return — and they won't be back this week, either. Skowronek suffered a calf injury early in the second quarter, and then Wilson injured his left hand on the final offensive drive of the first half. Wilson had a large wrap on his left hand after the game. On Monday, head coach Mike McCarthy said neither player will return to active this week. Fellow wide receiver DK Metcalf was initially listed as questionable to play after missing practice on Friday with an illness, but he has now been cleared to play. Tight end Pat Freiermuth is also questionable to play after suffering a calf injury in practice on Saturday. Strong safety DeShon Elliott remains limited in practice and will not return this week. Starting cornerback Jamel Dean was ruled out last week, but might be ahead of the curve on the initial multi-week estimate for his injury. He is listed as questionable. Running back Rico Dowdle , who is recovering from a dislocated toe on his left foot, is also questionable to make his return to the lineup, as is defensive tackle Keeanu Benton , who has an ankle injury, and defensive who has an ankle injury, and defensive back Jalen Ramsey , who has played through his broken wrist the last two weeks. A beat up Steelers defensive kept Tom Brady out of the end zone for 55 minutes and Mitch Trubisky successfully replaced an injury Kenny Pickett as Pittsburgh beat the Buccaneers, 20-18 at Acrisure Stadium on Oct. 16, 2022. Pickett threw his first career touchdown pass to Najee Harris in the first quarter, but a hit from blitzing linebacker Devin White knocked him out of the game. Chris Boswell kicked two field goals and Trubisky found Chase Claypool for a six-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to extend the Steelers lead. With 4:45 to play, Brady finally punched through a defense that was playing without T.J. Watt , Minkah Fitzpatrick , Ahkello Witherspoon , Levi Wallace and Cam Sutton with a touchdown pass to Leonard Fournette, but Devin Bush broke up the two-point conversion attempt, and Trubisky and the Pittsburgh offense ran out the clock. Defensive run game coordinator and outside linebackers coach Larry Foote had two stints with the Steelers, playing from 2002-08 and 2010-13 after the team made him a fifth-round draft pick out of Michigan. Foote was a two-time Super Bowl champion in Pittsburgh and also won a Super Bowl LV ring as a coach with Tampa in 2021. away.headline: Baker Mayfield Injury Update Doesn't Improve Buccaneers' Odds vs. Panthers in NFL Week 7
away.blurb: On the bright side for the Bucs, it appears that starting quarterback Baker Mayfield has a chance to return in Week 7. Mayfield, who dislocated his thumb in Week 3 against the Minnesota Vikings, appears to be nearing a return to practice, as NFL insider Tom Pelissero reported ahead of Week 6 that there is "optimism" that the former No. 1 overall pick will return against the Carolina Panthers. Pelissero: There's "optimism" that Baker Mayfield (thumb) will return Week 7. While that move could be a reaction to Sunday's results after Carolina picked up a win against Philadelphia, it's also possible that oddsmakers aren't quite sold on the Bucs getting their starting quarterback to return just yet. Mayfield needs to be able to grip and throw a football at a usual level before the team is going to send him out into a regular-season game. Baker Mayfield Injury Update Doesn't Improve Buccaneers' Odds vs. Panthers in NFL Week 7 Skip to main content ON SI The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are well outside the playoff picture in the NFC through six weeks, as they're just 1-5 after an overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels was unable to do enough to get the Bucs a second win in a row, and the team is in last place in the NFC South entering Week 7. That would be a major boost to a Tampa Bay team that needs a winning streak to get back in the mix to make the playoffs. Despite the report from Pelissero, oddsmakers aren't buying the Bucs on the road against the first-place Panthers and Bryce Young. Tampa Bay opened as a three-point underdog on the road in Week 7, and it has since moved to a 3.5-point underdog in the latest odds at DraftKings Sportsbook . At 1-5, the Bucs are +570 to make the playoffs and +12500 to win the Super Bowl, making them one of the bigger long shots in the NFL through six weeks. Mayfield has appeared in just three games and didn't exactly play at a high level, completing 63.5 percent of his passes for 615 yards, two scores and two picks before suffering the thumb injury. He's also carried the ball 11 times for 65 yards and a score this season. Tampa Bay's practice report on Wednesday should provide more insight into Mayfield's status for Week 7. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joe Burrow will riddle the Ravens' defense for 3 TD passes When the Bengals are right, they are tough on offense. And they've been cooking this year, ranking No. 9 in the NFL in points per game. Burrow is connecting on 71.4% of his passes. He has 11 touchdown passes and three interceptions. Look for him to keep the momentum going this week. But Burrow needs to take care of the football, which Zac Taylor said would go a long way in helping the Bengals win, according to Cleveland.com. "The turnovers is what screams at you," Taylor said. "That leads into field position." And Taylor said Burrow and his teammates are ready for this matchup. "It's exciting," Taylor said. "I think our guys really get fired up for this game. Not that they don't get fired up for every game, but whenever we play in Baltimore in a road divisional game, it's a fun one to get up for, and our guys will be up for it." Bengals RB Chase Brown will score two TDs One of them will be on the receiving end of a pass from Burrow. Brown will have a nice day, despite being caught in a time share with Samaje Perine, according to The Athletic. "I think we'll continually assess how that touch share between (Perine) and Chase Brown should play out," Bengals offensive coordinator Pitcher told Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "Every game's different. What type of scheme we lean into is going to factor into that. Obviously, what we ran more of yesterday leans into what Samaje does well, which is get downhill and run through contact." The Bengals haven't forgotten about their ground game. "You strive for balance when it comes to run-pass," Pitcher said. "You're always wanting to be the most balanced and versatile version of yourselves. It's like those are high-level goals that you set out to attain. But never in any given situation are we going to let a high-level theoretical goal get in the way of what it means on Sunday to win a game and what is the feedback we're getting in a game on a given Sunday." Derrick Henry will rush for 80-plus yards and a TD Henry is still smarting from last week's fumble that led to the Ravens' loss to the Browns. He took blame for the game-changing turnover , according to ESPN. "I got to take care of the ball," he said. "There's no excuses for that. I got to be better. I put the team in harm's way. I sound like a broken record with this, but I got to go back to work on it. Can't put the team in that situation." Teammate Kyle Hamilton took up for Henry. "Obviously, he's Derrick Henry, Hall of Fame running back [who] wants to hold onto the ball," Hamilton said. "He knows that. He's his harshest critic, so I'm not going to say anything ill about it. He's put us in position to win a lot of games." All of this will motivate Henry for a big game against the Bengals Ravens WR Ja'Kobi Lane will catch 5 passes and score a TD Lane looked ready to roll against the Browns in his return from injury. And he should be able to carve out a significant role in Week 7. Lane looked great in training camp. The injury short-circuited his 2026 season. But now he's back in the mix. His overall stat line could be impacted if Tyler Huntley is still at quarterback. But if Jackson is back, this could be a breakout game for Lane. Who will win the game? The Bengals should be able to outscore the Ravens in this matchup. But the key factor is Jackson. If he's back, the Ravens have a much better chance of winning. But we will still roll with Burrow, Chase, and Tee Higgins having a big game, along with Brown doing his thing. away.blurb: Nwokobia, an undrafted free agent out of SMU, originally signed with the Bengals in early May following the 2026 NFL Draft. With established safeties Bryan Cook, Jordan Battle, and Kyle Dugger ahead of him, plus depth pieces such as PJ Jules and the newly promoted Yeast, opportunities on the active roster have been limited for undrafted rookies. Nwokobia is now a free agent and eligible to sign with another team or return to Cincinnati should circumstances change. Eagles rule Jalen Hurts out for season amid blood clot issues Entertainment Entertainment Home ··· Boxing The Cincinnati Bengals released rookie safety Isaiah Nwokobia from the practice squad on Tuesday, according to a team announcement detailing multiple roster adjustments. The move came as the Bengals signed safety Russ Yeast from the practice squad to the active roster. Yeast fills a spot opened by tight end Tanner Hudson’s placement on injured reserve. To replenish the practice squad, Cincinnati signed tight end Josh Kattus and linebacker Emany Johnson. The 23-year-old from Dallas (Skyline High School) brought solid college production: career totals of 273 tackles, 11 interceptions (two returned for touchdowns), and 14 pass deflections across 53 games. He earned first-team All-ACC honors in 2024 after recording 100 tackles and three interceptions, and was named MVP of the 2023 American Athletic Conference Championship Game. His path with the Bengals has been uneven. The team waived him early in training camp on August 4 amid an undisclosed injury, with Nwokobia later reaching an injury settlement. He returned to the organization on September 29 when Cincinnati signed him to the practice squad after a workout. The latest release ends that stint. Nwokobia’s early camp release already suggested the Bengals viewed the position as relatively settled, and the current secondary depth appears to have left little room for further development on the practice squad. No specific reason for the practice-squad release was detailed beyond the corresponding roster moves. For a productive college safety who showed ball skills and tackling ability, the short NFL window underscores the steep competition at the position across the league. away.blurb: Wide receiver Colbie Young, a fourth-round pick out of Georgia, suffered a knee injury in week three and missed the Bengals' games against the Jacksonville Jaguars and Miami Dolphins. The Ravens face a significant injury report this week, as quarterback Lamar Jackson has missed the last two games, in which Baltimore went 1-1, beating the Atlanta Falcons and losing to the Cleveland Browns. Cincinnati is 3-2 and last in the division, while the Cleveland Browns, Pittsburgh Steelers, and Ravens are all 4-2. Cincinnati is getting in much better shape injury-wise. The week before the Miami Dolphins game, the Bengals were unsure whether Ja'Marr Chase, Tee Higgins , or Bryan Cook could play after earlier injuries. If he misses one or two more days, the question will be whether he's physically ready to play against the Ravens. Franchise QB Lamar Jackson has missed the last two games with an ankle injury, and backup Tyler Huntley has led the Ravens to a 1-1 record in Jackson's absence. Getty Tony Adame Wed, October 14, 2026 at 11:39 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Few defensive players are operating at the level of New York Giants edge rusher Abdul Carter right now, so any injury news on the 2025 No. 3 overall pick is cause for concern. That's why Carter's appearance on Wednesday's injury report for the Giants with a calf issue raised eyebrows — as did head coach John Harbaugh's predictably frosty response to questions about his health. Harbaugh was asked about Carter after he wasn't participating in Wednesday's practice. "John Harbaugh not providing any details on Abdul Carter beyond saying he will be on the injury report today," USA Today's Art Stapleton wrote on his official X account on Wednesday. "So we wait." Carter Putting Together Dominant Season Carter, 6-foot-3 and 252 pounds, has 14 tackles, 2.0 sacks, 2 TFLs, 6 QB hits, 17 QB pressures, and 1 forced fumble through 5 games for the Giants, who are 3-1-1 and, for the first time since 2015, alone in first place in the NFC East. The Giants host the New Orleans Saints in Week 6. "Abdul Carter will be on the injury report but he's doing well, coach John Harbaugh said," ESPN's Jordan Raanan wrote on his official X account on Wednesday. "I'm not expecting it to be anything overly concerning." Giants Already Lost One Elite Edge Rusher Carter's high level of play comes after the Giants suffered a crushing blow early in the season when NFL All-Pro edge rusher Brian Burns suffered a season-ending knee injury in a Week 3 win over the Tennessee Titans . Burns, who is playing on a 5-year, $141 million contract, finished second in the NFL with 18.5 sacks in 2025 and earned NFL All-Pro honors for the first time. away.blurb: The Giants ruled out safety Tyler Nubin (neck), tight end Theo Johnson (neck), and cornerback Colton Hood (concussion). WR Chris Olave (illness) didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to work on a limited basis during Friday's practice. He should play so long as that illness is behind him. DL Nathan Shepherd (illness) also missed two days of practice with an illness that's been going around the locker room. He was limited on Friday as well. CB Lorenzo Styles Jr. (knee) was limited on both Thursday and Friday, so don't be surprised if he's a game-time decision. RB Alvin Kamara (back) practiced on limited reps throughout the week. The Saints didn't bring up either of the two running b acks on their practice squad so it does llook like he'll play. Starting offensive linemen Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are both questionable for the Giants, as is edge rusher Abdul Carter (calf). There's a crowd of Giants players available to play after being listed on the injury report this week: cornerback Greg Newsome II (groin), outside linebacker Malik Harrison (groin), defensive back Elijah Campbell (thumb), running back Najee Harris (ribs), tight end Isaiah Likely (foot), wide receivers Darnell Mooney (neck) and Charlie Jones (Achilles), as well as safety Jason Pinnock (concussion). As was the case last week, the following Saints players are on injured reserve with season-ending injuries: defensive tackle Bryan Bresee, running back Ty Chandler, cornerback David Long Jr., tight end Moliki Matavao, offensive lineman Dillon Radunz, and cornerback Rejzohn Wright. home.headline: Why Tank Dell coming back creates a good problem for Houston Texans
home.blurb: This moment may have seemed like it was never going to come. Almost two years ago, Tank Dell suffered a severe leg injury that put his career in jeopardy. Now, 22 months later, Dell is ready to return to a Houston Texans team that is plenty deep at the wide receiver position. The Texans are expecting Dell to return to action this weekend against the New York Giants. He hasn’t played since December of 2024 when he was carted off the field with multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap. It was a devastating injury that left quarterback C.J. Stroud visibly shaken, and put the former 3rd round pick’s future in jeopardy. Now he is back and while DeMeco Ryans is excited, he knows that Dell will have to take things slow. “I expect Tank just to be himself and just play the offense the right way,” coach DeMeco Ryans said on Monday. “No huge expectations from what he needs to do. We’re all just going to be excited. I know me personally, I’m just going to be excited to see him just out there for the first time in over two years, just getting some game action. I’m just thankful, grateful for him to have this opportunity to return. I don’t have any expectations. I’m just happy to see him out there and that’s the only thing that matters.” It’s might be an embarrassment of riches for coach Ryans, but he will take all he can get after his team started the year 0-4. They have won two off the rip, and brought in Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Arizona Cardinals, and now the return of Dell gives them an added weapon for Stroud and the passing game. Dell ended up tearing multiple ligaments , sustained meniscus damage and dislocated his left knee in the incident. It knocked him out of the entire 2025 campaign, and he's been recovering ever since. Dell had 667 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 14 games during the 2024 campaign. The Texans selected him in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Houston. Though it's unclear if Dell will be able to compete at the same level he was at previously, considering how significant his knee injury and rehab actually was, he's finally ready to get back out onto the field. The next part of his playing career is here. Ryan Young Staff writer Mon, October 19, 2026 at 8:13 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Houston Texans wide receiver will take the field on Sunday for their matchup with the New York Giants, head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed on Monday. It will mark Dell's first game back since he went down with a gruesome knee injury in 2024. Dell caught a deep pass from quarterback C.J. Stroud in a matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs in December 2024. But as Dell was bringing the ball in, teammate Jared Wayne dove for the ball too and accidentally crashed into Dell's left knee. Dell made the catch, and completed the 30-yard touchdown, but the injury was gruesome. He had to be driven off the field on a stretcher in what was a very emotional scene at Arrowhead Stadium. He remained in a Kansas City-area hospital overnight, and returned to Houston the next day. The injury was just the latest significant one that Dell has already faced in his career. His rookie season was cut short after he fractured his fibula just 11 games in, and he was then shot in the leg as a bystander at a mass shooting in Florida in 2024. Dell recovered from both injuries in time to start the 2024 campaign normally. Dell will rejoin the Texans at a critical time for the organization this season, too. After losing four straight to start the year, they've now won back-to-back contests entering Sunday's matchup with the Giants at NRG Stadium. They most recently rallied to beat the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday.

picks.blurb: Denver Broncos at Arizona Cardinals preview: Denver aims for 3-game win streak | Mile High Report Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Denver Broncos Community Mile High Report October 21, 2026 Mile High Report Notifications Notifications Sections News By/For Fans The Feed Community Guidelines Today's Trivia Betting Betting News FanDuel NFL Odds FanDuel Super Bowl Odds Denver Broncos Odds NFL Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search Sections Expand News By/For Fans Expand The Feed Betting Expand Betting News All communities Notifications Denver Broncos Game Information The Broncos are coming off a big win over Seattle and the mini-bye for their game against the Cardinals on Sunday. Bo Nix and the Denver Broncos are coming off a huge win over the defending Super Bowl champs. Next on the docket is a scrappy Arizona Cardinals bunch that just pulled a huge road upset of the Los Angeles Rams. The good news for the Broncos (4-2) is that they got the mini-bye week before heading to the desert and could get a few players back from injury and the commissioner’s exempt list. Denver looks to extend its winning streak to three games after coming out of a gauntlet to start the season. The Broncos are currently -4.5-point road favorites over Arizona (2-4). The total sits at over/under 43.5 points, with a lean toward the over at -115. Offensive Rankings Denver : Thirty-first in total offense (252.2 yards per game), 26th in rushing offense (84.2 YPG), 28th in passing offense (168.0 YPG), 26th in scoring offense (19.0 points per game). Arizona : Twenty-third in total offense (307.3 yards per game), 22nd in rushing offense (96.3 YPG), 20th in passing offense (211.0 YPG), 24th in scoring offense (21.0 points per game). Defensive Rankings Denver : Twenty-second in total defense (348.3 yards per game), 31st in rushing defense (139.8 YPG), 10th in passing defense (208.5 YPG), tied for 10th in scoring defense (20.8 points per game). Arizona : Twenty-third in total defense (350.5 yards per game), 20th in rushing defense (120.8 YPG), 22nd in passing defense (229.7 YPG), tied for 31st in scoring defense (29.7 points per game). Here are the MHR staff’s keys to Sunday’s game. Win the line of scrimmage on offense The Broncos offensive line has been the definition of “meh” to start the regular season. It’s nowhere near what it’s been the last few seasons, but it also isn’t horrid either. Denver needs to dominate the line of scrimmage on Sunday. Open lanes in the running game and do a better job of pass protection. It’s a cliche, but success on offense starts in the trenches. Getting that could lay the foundation for jump-starting the offense. — Ian St. Clair Bench Bo Nix; Start Jarrett Stidham Just kidding. Ya’ll crazy if you think benching Bo Nix is even remotely the answer. That said, Bo Nix does need to play better, and he isn’t seeing the field well to start the season. He’s had slow starts in every season he’s played, so, for now, I’m chalking this up to another slow start. However, seven games in, I’m hoping to see him take flight a bit now that the hardest part of the Broncos’ schedule is complete. At 4-2, they got through it with a winning record, and that is all we could hope for. — Tim Lynch Pressure the QB The key to this game is the same as it has been every week. Get to the QB. The defense has done a great job this season of causing mayhem in the backfield. Make it uncomfortable for Jacoby Brissett (like the back of a Volkswagen). When QBs are harassed and hurried, they make mistakes. — Adam Malnati Disciplined, execution-based offensive football This team needs to execute at a high level, and it will win this game easily. The defense is already there. If the offense can up its game, this Broncos team will be unstoppable. — Sadaraine Limit the impact of Trey McBride The Broncos defense has performed well this season, aside from a few games. For the most part, they’ve been able to limit the impact of the opposing team’s top player on their offense. This week, they face All-Pro tight end Trey McBride, who is coming off a sensational 2025 season. He is the focal point of Arizona’s aerial attack and gets over ten targets per game. Defensive coordinator Vance Joseph needs to come up with a good game plan that limits his impact on the game. If they can slow him down, Denver will have a great shot at earning their fifth victory of the season. — Christopher Hart What are your keys to Sunday’s game? away.headline: Week 6 Injury Report: Seahawks at Broncos
away.blurb: Among those practicing fully on Wednesday was receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who was listed as limited the previous two days because of an ankle injury. Smith-Njigba, who leads the NFL in receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, does not have a game status on the final injury report, meaning he is good to go. Also without a status, despite being listed as limited all week with an ankle injury, is defensive lineman Leonard Williams, who played last week through the injury he suffered in a Week 4 win over the Chargers. Also ruled out are linebacker Chazz Surratt, who will miss a third straight game with a calf injury, and running back Zach Charbonnet, who remains on the physically unable to perform list as he works his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in last season's Divisional Round win over the 49ers. For the Broncos, All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II has been ruled out with an ankle injury, as has starting safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle). Starting cornerback Riley Moss, who missed last weekend's game with a rib injury, is questionable after being listed as limited in practice all week. RB Zach Charbonnet (knee, limited participation) CB Riley Moss (ribs, limited participation) Tuesday's injury report, which like Monday's is an estimation of participation, was mostly unchanged from a day earlier. Guard Beau Stephens (shoulder) went from being listed as limited Monday to full participation Tuesday, while every other player's status stayed the same. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the NFL's leading receiver, was listed as limited for the second straight day due to an ankle injury, as was defensive tackle Leonard Williams. Receiver Irv Charles, who was activated from injured reserve earlier in the day, was again listed as a full participant, another indicator that he is on track to make his Seahawks debut on Thursday. For the Broncos, two starters in the secondary, cornerback Patrick Surtain II (ankle) and safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) were listed as non-participants for the second straight day. home.blurb: Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB OUT For Week 6 Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB’s Week 6 Status Revealed - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Jeremiyah Love Injury Update: Cardinals RB’s Week 6 Status Revealed Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Jeremiyah Love has battled an ankle injury throughout the season, and the ailment will keep the running back sidelined for Week 6. The Arizona Cardinals gave him the most guaranteed money of any running back in NFL history when they selected him with the third-overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft , and it's easy to see why. The Notre Dame product dominated at the collegiate level, routinely flashing his elite athleticism and ability to make plays both as a runner and a returner. In theory, he has the talent to be a true three-down workhorse like Atlanta's Bijan Robinson and Detroit's Jahmyr Gibbs . Unfortunately for everyone involved, Jeremiyah Love suffered an ankle injury during his first real taste of NFL action. The running back suffered an ankle injury midway through the contest and missed most of the preseason. While he has played in five games despite the injury, NFL Network's Ian Rapoport revealed the running back will not play in Week 6, as the team is resting him in hopes of ensuring his long-term health. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - David Latham, Managing Editor While Jeremiyah Love has played in every game this season, he hasn't lived up to his pre-draft hype. So far, the running back has recorded just 245 yards and one touchdown on 67 attempts, good for just 3.7 yards per carry. While the Cardinals passing attack and subpar offensive line certainly haven't done anything to ease the pressure on the rookie, he hasn't looked like his college self either. Hopefully, taking some time to rest will help him recapture his previous form. In his absence, free agent signee Tyler Allgeier will get the start. The former Atlanta Falcon has had similar struggles behind Arizona's offensive line, recording just 119 yards and one touchdown on 35 attempts throughout the young season. home.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals opened their practice week Wednesday for Sunday’s road game against the Los Angeles Rams and released their first injury report of Week 5. Running back Jeremiyah Love did not practice. It appeared that LaFleur claimed Williams would be unavailable for Sunday’s game when he said, “He’s not going to clear the concussion protocol.” The report is an estimate because the Rams did not practice after playing the Buffalo Bills Monday night. Recovered from the right high-ankle sprain suffered in the Aug. 13 preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders , his left ankle has been an issue for several weeks. He has felt good heading into games, but then aggravation occurs on the field. Head coach Mike LaFleur said, “Want to get this ankle right and do it the right way. He’s a tough dude. You guys see the way he plays and how aggressive he is with his cuts. Imagine being a running back in the NFL, trying to put the foot down and cut the way that you’re capable of. We all are in agreeance, as much as he wants to battle through, we’re all in agreeance right now that (he needs to) give a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on what that’ll entail for Sunday.” Asked about concern about it continuing to be a problem going forward, LaFleur said, “It’s an ankle, so you don’t know. I’m not a doctor and each body is a little bit different. The way he came back from the one in the preseason was unbelievable. He doesn’t even feel it, but this one is the one that happened when the regular season started and it’s just lingering.” The full details their Wednesday injury repory are below. The Packers opened the week as underdogs, getting 1.5 points at most sportsbooks, but the line quickly flipped to Packers -1.5 by Monday morning. Then, once the dust settled and the game approached, at least a handful of books had switched back to having the Cowboys favored. Green Bay took the season opener at Lambeau Field 27-13, then got another Thanksgiving Day victory in Detroit in a high-scoring, 31-24 affair. Prior to 2025, the 2020 season was the last time Green Bay went 2-for-2, when they won similarly high scoring games in weeks 2 (42-24) and 14 (also 31-24). If you are navigating lineup decisions ahead of Sunday afternoon's kickoff, here is a breakdown of which Lions fantasy superstars belong in your starting lineup, and which options require a bit more caution. Must-Start Locks Amon-Ra St. Brown (WR) * Verdict: Mandatory Start (WR1) * The Outlook: St. Brown remains the unquestioned heart of Detroit's passing attack.
