Green Bay's secondary has struggled at times against refined route runners over the middle. Expect Jared Goff to lean heavily on his favorite target to sustain drives, making St. Brown an elite WR1 in all PPR formats. Jahmyr Gibbs (RB) * Verdict: Mandatory Start (RB1) * The Outlook: Gibbs' dual-threat dynamic explosion makes him virtually matchup-proof. With his elite speed on Ford Field's turf, he only needs a handful of touches to break open a slate. The Packers have surrendered chunk plays to explosive pass-catching tailbacks out of the backfield, giving Gibbs immense ceiling potential in PPR and half-PPR leagues. High-Upside Starts Jared Goff (QB) * Verdict: Solid QB1 Start * The Outlook: Goff inside the friendly confines of Ford Field is one of the safest fantasy plays on the board. At home, Goff operates Drew Petzing' system with supreme efficiency and rhythm. While Green Bay's pass rush can generate pressure, Goff's quick-release capabilities and weapons across the field give him a safe 18–22 point fantasy floor with multi-touchdown upside. Start with Caution / Situational Starts Jameson Williams (WR) * Verdict: High-Risk Boom-or-Bust Flex * The Outlook: Williams possesses game-breaking speed capable of turning a single target into a 70-yard touchdown. If you need pure upside to pull off an upset in your matchup, roll the dice on Williams; if you require a steady double-digit floor, explore alternative options. Sam LaPorta (TE) * Verdict: Low-End TE1 / High-End TE2 * The Outlook: LaPorta continues to command valuable red-zone attention, but increased target competition across the offense has capped his weekly target share. Green Bay's linebackers and safeties play tough physical coverage against tight ends over the middle. He remains startable given the top-heavy nature of the tight end position, but manage expectations accordingly. Final Lineup Verdict Lock in your top-tier Lions stars without hesitation. Detroit's high-octane offense inside Ford Field provides plenty of fantasy production to go around. Fire up St. Brown, Gibbs, Goff with confidence as Detroit aims to defend home turf against their division rivals.

picks.headline: Packers vs. Lions predictions: Detroit's biggest weakness could decide Week 7
picks.blurb: Detroit scores points like no other, but also gives them up at an alarming rate. In other words, Christian Watson and Matthew Golden should be salivating at the matchup. The fantasy managers who roster those players will be thinking the same thing. More importantly, this is a key contest in the ever-crowded NFC North where there is no margin for error. Green Bay enters the contest at 4-2, erasing any negative thoughts that surfaced after the 0-2 start to the year. Detroit is 3-2, which is good enough for last place in the NFC North. Both teams are chasing the 5-0 Vikings , with the 4-2 Bears standing in the way as well. With only so many playoff spots to go around, this Week 7 matchup could have massive implications down the road. Here's a look at the keys to the game, injuries to watch and a prediction. Lions vs Packers odds, moneyline, over/under Opening lines: Spread: Lions -2.5 Moneyline: Lions -142; Packers +120 Get the edge with our exclusive NFL betting picks Lions Keys To Victory Slow down Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. It's easier said than done, of course, but it's the one true path to victory for Detroit - outside of winning a shootout. The Lions' secondary has been a huge weakness all season long, and perhaps there is no better team position to exploit that than the Packers. Green Bay will try to hit some home runs with its speedy receivers. Even with Brian Branch set to return, Detroit will have to be willing to sit back in zone coverage and hold the visitors to some singles. Packers Keys To Victory Stay patient. With a defense as weak as the Lions, the Packers just have to play the waiting game. And that's something Dan Campbell's teams haven't been known to do. Detroit can either take away the long ball or attempt to get to Jordan Love with pressure. If the Lions sit back, then the Packers need to show an ability to run the ball. If they pressure, get ready to light up the scoreboard. Green Bay has the advantage, but it can't beat itself. Injuries to watch • S Brian Branch • OL Cade Mays • OL Aaron Banks. Lions vs Packers USA TODAY expert picks Nicholas Brinkerhoff: Packers 34, Lions 30 This game might come down to who has the ball last. Detroit might be coming out of the bye with some reinforcements, but this is still a defense that will ruin a season. And for that reason, no lead is safe - especially against the rival Packers, who can strike quickly. Jordan Love was forced to grow up as a quarterback without a running game to rely on through the first six weeks. He is passing that test with flying colors after a slow start. Trust the more well-rounded Packers to get the job done and push their winning streak to four. Adam Kaufman: Lions 31, Packers 27 This should be fun. Green Bay has won three straight, but Detroit comes out of its bye with reinforcements. Brian Branch's expected return won't magically fix the secondary, though even a few additional stops could make a significant difference. The Lions already have an offense capable of taking advantage, with Jahmyr Gibbs headlining their weapons. Jordan Love should still find opportunities, and the Packers can absolutely win if they protect him and avoid giving the home team extra possessions. Josh Jacobs' availability is another important piece. I'm expecting both quarterbacks to have productive stretches. But Jared Goff and Dan Campbell have been a dynamic duo with extended rest and know what's at stake in a crowded NFC North. This should be competitive well into the fourth quarter, but I like the Lions indoors. Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley was hired to be the next head coach of the Miami Dolphins, and Green Bay hired Jonathan Gannon (previously the head coach of the Cardinals) as a replacement. With Gannon came a new 3-4 defense and a whole bunch of changes on the defensive side of the ball. EDGE Rashan Gary was traded to the Cowboys, NT Colby Wooden was traded to the Colts, while EDGE Kingsley Enagbare, MIKE Quay Walker, and CB Nate Hobbs departed in free agency. EDGE/LB Micah Parsons continues to recover from an ACL tear and is not expected to be available in Week 7. Being up against the cap, the Packers elected to promote from within, inserting EDGE Lukas Van Ness and ILB Isaiah McDuffie into the starting lineup, trading for LB Zaire Franklin (who is starting in place of injured Edgerrin Cooper), and drafting starters CB Brandon Cisse (second round) and NT Chris McClellan (third) on Day 2 of the NFL Draft. On offense, the Packers lost QB Malik Willis, RB Emanuel Wilson, WR Dontayvion Wicks (traded to the Eagles), WR Romeo Dobbs, LT Rasheed Walker, and LG/C Elgton Jenkins; like on defense, they elected to mostly promote from within, elevating RB Marshawn Lloyd into a bigger role (especially with Josh Jacobs suspended—he is expected to return in Week 7), WR Savion Williams and LT Jordan Morgan into the starting lineup, and shifting Sean Rhyan inside to center. Their guard spots have been a massive problem, and the Packers have been searching for answers, with their most recent pairing being RG Travis Glover and former Lion LG Laken Tomlinson (starting in place of the injured Aaron Banks). After a slow start to their 2026 season, the Packers have settled down as their offense has found its groove. The Packers opened the season with a loss after allowing the Vikings to drop 39 points on them, rebounded in Week 2 by beating the Jets by three points, only to lose again in Week 3 as the Falcons dominated them on the ground to the tune of 35 points. In Week 4, the Packers once again found a way to win by three points, this time over the Bucs, then smashed a Caleb Williams-less Bears team 31-7. In Week 6, the Packers took on the Cowboys’ 31st-ranked defense on “Sunday Night Football,” and while they jumped out to a 17-0 lead in the first half, they only scored six points in the second half. Fortunately, their defense held strong and allowed only 13 points, and the game ended in a 23-13 win. With the Packers offense in a groove, the Lions secondary is certainly going to be tested. Will they be able to carry over the success they had against the Cardinals in Week 5? Will Brian Branch return? If so, how big of a factor will he be? With so much unknown about the Lions’ defense, there’s a real chance the Packers continue their run of putting up points, and Detroit will need their top-scoring offense to keep pace and lead the Lions to victory. away.headline: Packers-Cowboys Thursday Injury Report: (Really) Big Help on the Way
away.blurb: Riley was designated for return from the PUP list on Wednesday and went through his second practice on Thursday. While he probably will need more than one week of practice, he will be a huge asset – literally and figuratively – whenever he’s cleared for game action. “Definitely rusty,” he said after being limited participation at practice. “Just trying to knock the rust off. We got a saying, ‘Got to vs. get to.’ I get to get coached. I get to get those reps in practice, which are very expensive, as I like to say, expensive reps. So, I take those very seriously and it's been good. I’m good physically. No sores or aches. I’m just in a good spot. Taking it day by day at a time.” “Man, it sucks, but it’s part of the business,” he said. “It’s part of the game we play. We love to play. You can’t really be so stuck on the past. You just got to continue to look forward, so when it happened, I just knew I’m going to recover from an Achilles injury. Few seconds to get down a little bit, but after that’s over, the emotion’s over, I told myself I’m going to return from an Achilles injury.” The Packers need help on the defensive line. It was one of their strongest positions coming out of training camp but Warren Brinson is on injured reserve and he’ll soon be joined by Hargrave. That leaves the Packers with only five players at a position group in which coordinator Jonathan Gannon prefers to rotate players in and out of the lineup. “That is above me,” he said of his potential return. “I just stick on one day at a time. Today, we had padded practice, so that’s what my focus was on – padded practice today. No really looking forward; just taking it each day at a time.” Cornerback Keisean Nixon and defensive tackle Jonathan Ford did not practice on Wednesday. Nixon returned on Thursday and was limited participation. Coach Matt LaFleur before practice said “I would expect (Ford) to be out there today,” but, while he went through the pre-practice warmup, he officially did not practice. Ford, who has played in all five games with one start, could be in for a heavier workload following Javon Hargrave’s torn Achilles if healthy. He’s averaged 23 snaps per game. If he can’t play and Riley isn’t ready, the Packers would have only four defensive tackles available. Nixon and safety Evan Williams (illness), who went from limited participation on Wednesday to full participation on Thursday, were the only changes. St-Juste, Ford, Hargrave and receiver/returner Skyy Moore (ankle) did not practice. For the Cowboys, only one starter did not practice on Wednesday due to injury. That was linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, who missed the last four games with a hamstring injury. He progressed to limited participation on Thursday. Only cornerback Cobie Durant (hamstring) and offensive tackle Drew Shelton (hamstring) did not practice for Dallas, which is coming off a Thursday night game so is well-rested. home.blurb: Detroit got a head start on the week, moving their first practice from Wednesday to Tuesday, a common practice from this regime out of a bye week. According to coach Dan Campbell, it also served the purpose of giving returning players Brian Branch and Cade Mays a big load of work, then giving them—and the rest of the team—Wednesday off to let their bodies recover. And if Tuesday’s practice is any indication, the Lions will be entering this pivotal Week 7 matchup with a good bill of health. Not only will Branch and Mays make their 2026 debuts for the team, but Detroit’s Tuesday practice had every single player on the active roster practicing. That includes the return of reserve cornerback Rock Ya-Sin, who had missed last game with a hamstring injury. Now, it wouldn’t be completely accurate to call the Lions “fully healthy” at this point in the season. Just last week, the Lions placed three players—WR Tom Kennedy, G Ben Bartch, and LB Devin White—on injured reserve , with Kennedy out for the season and White out for at least a couple of months with a broken forearm. Beyond that, the Lions still have Isiah Pacheco, Kendrick Law, Avonte Maddox, and Thomas Harper on injured reserve as well. home.headline: It's now or never for Lions' defense with Brian Branch's return imminent
home.blurb: It's now or never for Lions' defense with Brian Branch's return imminent Skip to main content News The return of safety Brian Branch is a critical point for this defense. If it shows some improvement with its do-it-all DB back in the lineup from a torn Achilles, the Lions have something to build on. That should make them buyers at the November 10 trade deadline. If it's still among the NFL's worst units, then Detroit can basically kiss any hopes of meaningful contention goodbye. The defense has been flat-out unworkable in multiple games this season. Before last week, it ranked near the bottom of the league in most conventional and advanced statistics. Brian Branch's imminent return could help transform Lions' defense This was what the Lions needed to see entering their bye week with one of their most impactful players potentially nearing a return. Abney hadn't played safety since middle school, and almost exclusively played outside cornerback in college. But the Lions tried him at nickel before kicking him back to safety against Arizona – partly out of necessity and partly because it couldn't get any worse. The Detroit Lions' defense is about to have a make-or-break moment. The Lions still allow the most yards per game in the NFL and the fourth-highest points per game. But yes, last Sunday's win over the lowly Arizona Cardinals was a good sign of a turnaround – or at the very least, that Detroit has nowhere to go but up defensively. The Lions sacked quarterback Jacoby Brissett five times, and he completed just 29 of his 47 passing attempts. Arizona rushed for just 56 yards as a team on 18 attempts. Yes, the Cardinals are one of the worst teams in the NFL. But the Lions were at a point, following their loss to the Carolina Panthers, where it looked like their defense was going to get in trouble from just about every offense in the NFL. After a slow first-quarter start, it's nice to see any encouraging results from this unit. "I thought we were sticky in coverage, very disciplined minus a couple of plays there," head coach Dan Campbell said . "I thought (defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard) and the staff did an outstanding job and the players really responded, man. They took it to heart and tried to do all the little things right, and play with aggressiveness, and just really set the tone for the day." Branch is a Swiss Army knife to the extreme on defense. His fusion of man coverage stickiness, zone coverage feel, blitz ferocity, sure tackling, and run defense instincts is unmatched by just about anyone in the NFL. Offenses absolutely have to know where he is. His versatility makes everyone on the Lions' defense's job easier. When he's at his best, Branch is a truly transformative player. It doesn't seem like fellow safety Kerby Joseph is returning from his mysterious knee injury anytime soon, or ever. That means Branch could be paired with rookie Keith Abney at safety. picks.blurb: NFL Week 7 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Chiefs upend Seahawks, Raiders scare Rams Skip to main content NFL NFL Standings NFL Free Agency NFL News by Team More NFL News Our NFL Sites MLB Standings MLB Trades and Transactions MLB Free Agency Baseball Insiders MLB News by Team More MLB News Our MLB Sites Draft Tracker NBA Free Agency NBA Standings NBA News by Team More NBA News Our NBA Sites Anaheim Ducks Boston Bruins Buffalo Sabres Calgary Flames Carolina Hurricanes Chicago Blackhawks Colorado Avalanche Columbus Blue Jackets Detroit Red Wings Edmonton Oilers Florida Panthers Los Angeles Kings Minnesota Wild Montreal Canadiens Nashville Predators New Jersey Devils New York Islanders New York Rangers Ottawa Senators Philadelphia Flyers Pittsburgh Penguins San Jose Sharks Seattle Kraken St. Louis Blues Tampa Bay Lightning Toronto Maple Leafs Vancouver Canucks Vegas Golden Knights Washington Capitals Winnipeg Jets COLLEGE College Football Men's College Basketball Women's College Basketball Men's College Baseball ABOUT Contact Meet the Editorial Team Our Entertainment Sites The Kansas City Chiefs have been as reliable as possible, the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams have not, the Las Vegas Raiders seem like they just won't go away, and it's safe to say the regular season has gotten off to a wild and weird start as we head into NFL Week 7 . Our picks and predictions each week have been indicative of that. Sorry I didn't have the Arizona Cardinals beating the Rams outright or the Tennessee Titans getting their first win of the season. We persevere and keep going with the picks. It's going to be a fun Week 7 in the league, as the NFL has big-time matchups like Cowboys-Eagles (less exciting than it once was), Chiefs-Seahawks, Rams-Raiders, Packers-Lions and even Patriots-Bears on Thursday night. That's enough to set the stage alone, so let's get right into our NFL Week 7 picks with predictions straight-up and against the spread for every game this week. NFL Week 7 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL Week 7 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Patriots vs. Bears (TNF) Steelers vs. Saints (Paris) Buccaneers vs. Panthers Panthers -3.5 49ers vs. Falcons Bengals vs. Ravens Giants vs. Texans Dolphins vs. Jets Browns vs. Titans Colts vs. Vikings Broncos vs. Cardinals Cardinals +4.5 Rams vs. Raiders Packers vs. Lions Chiefs vs. Seahawks Cowboys vs. Eagles 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 58-35 (Last week 7-7) | ATS Record: 43-48-2 (Last week 6-8) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 7 prediction to make Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Kansas City Chiefs (+2.5) vs. Seattle Seahawks Frankly, there were a lot of tough predictions to make, but taking the Chiefs to go on the road to Seattle and hand the Seahawks another loss outright feels like the one I struggled with the most. With all due respect to the 12th Man and the impact that could have on this game, there's a lot to be worried about when it comes to the Seahawks right now. Sam Darnold and this offense are in dire straits, particularly with their inability to effectively run the ball, which then puts it all on the shoulders of a quarterback who, outside of the playoffs last year, has been exceptionally turnover-prone. That then, in turn, puts way too much pressure on this defense. Then there's the Chiefs, a team that has a defense under Steve Spagnuolo that feels tailor-made to be able to put Darnold into turnover-prone positions in this game. Now, to be sure, the Kansas City passing offense hasn't been operating on all cylinders, so I do wonder what Mike Macdonald will have in store to try and bottle up Kenneth Walker III. At the end of the day, though, there's simply more I trust with the Chiefs right now than with Seahawks, so even on the road, give me KC. Easiest NFL Week 7 pick on the board New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Don't mistake this for having any type of unwavering faith in the New York Jets. It's wavering quite a bit. At the same time, maybe the thing that I'm most confident in right now is the fact that the Miami Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL. Yes, they might win a game randomly at some point this season, but I have a hard time believing that win comes on the road and that it comes against a team that is at least as healthy as the Jets are right now in this moment. The Dolphins don't have anyone that can cover Garrett Wilson or even Omar Cooper Jr. in the passing game, which should give Geno Smith some consistent options in the pass game, while Braelon Allen and the offensive line are getting the run game clicking. The defense is fine overall, but the pass rush against a team that's not without De'Von Achane leads me to believe that Malik Willis is going to have a tough time on Sunday. This feels almost too simple, but I can't pass it up. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) I know, I know, I know. My Bo Nix slander has gone entirely too far. I can hear you complaining about it now, and it's a fair point, because even after beating the Rams, I'm under no guise that the Cardinals are a high-quality football team. At the same time, though, Nix is playing like the worst quarterback in the NFL right now. Even as someone low on Nix, I didn't expect this type of dramatic dropoff with no real signs of things getting any better. The Cardinals defense is certainly a generous unit, but I don't know if Sean Payton or Nix himself have enough faith in the quarterback right now to fully take advantage of that. Moreover, the defense has, on the whole, been lesser than a year ago and has been quite banged up. While the ceiling of the Cardinals is low, I don't think that Jacoby Brissett is going to make the same back-breaking mistakes we saw Sam Darnold make on Thursday Night Football last week. This feels like a game that could end up being similarly weird to Arizona's win over the Rams this past week, and I'm not only taking the Cards against the spread in this matchup, but give me them to pull off the upset fully while playing at home. McVay said during media availability that he is "feeling good" and they are merely "erring on the side of caution." McVay did not outright state that Allen would be out there for the game, but the third and final injury report could reveal more about his chances to play. Linebacker Nate Landman (shoulder), tight end Colby Parkinson (shoulder), and cornerback Josh Wallace (shoulder) also remained limited through Thursday's practice. McVay also commented on Trost, stating that the rookie lineman will test out his ability to suit up for the game. Considering he has been out of action since the first game of preseason, he may need time to ramp back up t o football activities. Safety Kam Curl was also added to the injury report on Thursday, as he was limited due to an ankle injury. Left tackle Alaric Jackson will be out for the game after being suspended. The lineman was involved in an incident on Monday night after the loss to the Buffalo Bills, where he punched Bills defender Bradley Chubb in the face. With Jackson out, the Rams will rely on David Quessenberry to start at the left tackle position. It may have been Trost stepping in, but he might also need more time to ramp up and be available. (Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images) James Brizuela Fri, October 16, 2026 at 2:53 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Los Angeles Rams have released their second injury report, and tight end Davis Allen has missed a second straight practice. However, head coach Sean McVay stated that its merely a precaution as opposed to be something significant. Allen remains the only worry on the list. The full injry report is as follows: Linebacker Omar Speights (knee) was a full participant, as were Keagen Trost (hamstring), and wide receiver Alex Bachman (wrist). The Rams do not have a ton of worries on their injury report and could be mostly at full strength when they face the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6. However, they will be without one important player. That punch led to a two-game suspension for Jackson, which was officially reduced to one game after a successful appeal. Should Trost make it into the game, he would presumably act as the backup tackle to Quessenberry, should anything happen to the veteran. The Rams are currently 2-3 this season and need a big win on Sunday. Falling to 2-4 might point to some bigger issues with the team and their chances of truly capturing the NFC West title at the end of the season.

According to the NFL, the incident occurred with 1:32 left in the fourth quarter after the Raiders' extra point attempt. Franklin denies the incident ever happened and is planning to appeal, according to WGR550's Sal Capaccio . Franklin is the second Bills player this week to be suspended for a spitting incident against the Raiders. The league announced Monday that C.J. Gardner-Johnson will miss a game after spitting on the ground toward the feet of Raiders tight end Brock Bowers. home.headline: Bills' Sam Franklin Jr. Suspended by NFL for Spitting at Raiders, Joins CJGJ in Missing Week 8
home.blurb: Buffalo Bills defensive back Sam Franklin Jr. landed in some hot water for an incident during the team's Week 6 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. The NFL announced that Franklin has been suspended for one game for "an act of unsportsmanlike conduct" after he was seen spitting at an opponent in the fourth quarter of Sunday's game. The Bills are on a bye this week, so Franklin will miss their Week 8 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens. According to ESPN's Adam Schefter , Franklin "is denying the allegation and will appeal." Franklin joined the Bills' practice squad prior to the 2025 season and quickly earned a spot on the main roster. He appeared in all 17 games last season, mostly on special teams. He was voted a team captain this season. While Franklin is denying the allegation, it seems like the Bills had a hard time keeping their mouths shut during Sunday's contest. Veteran safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson also received a one-game suspension after cameras caught him spitting toward Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and center Tyler Linderbaum. "C.J. knows that it's hard enough to win in this league with 48 guys, much less 47. He knows that that can't happen. It's inexcusable. That's not the standard that we're going to have and play with," Bills head coach Joe Brady told reporters on Monday. "He's addressed it. It's been addressed. The league came down with the suspension. … We want to toe the line with everything we do but we can't cross the line." Gardner-Johnson addressed the incident with his teammates and coaches after the game, and he posted an apology for his actions on social media. "My passion and competitive nature have always been a huge part of who I am, but I also understand that there is a line that should never be crossed," he wrote. "The gesture I made toward my opponent was inappropriate, unnecessary, and not a reflection of the respect I have for him or this game." The Bills will try to focus on avoiding any further incidents during their bye week before returning to action on Nov. 1 against the Ravens.

Seattle is coming off a bad loss to Denver on Thursday Night Football in Week 6, as Sam Darnold threw multiple picks and the Seattle offense struggled to get anything going against an elite Denver defense. That dropped the Seahawks to 3-3, and they’re multiple games out of first place in the NFC West. Meanwhile, the Kansas City defense put on a clinic in Week 6, holding the Los Angeles Chargers to just six points to move to 5-0 in the 2026 season. There is a huge revenge game possibly on Sunday, as Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III returns to Seattle for the first time since he won Super Bowl MVP for the ‘Hawks. The Seahawks let the star back go in free agency, and he’s been a monster for the Chiefs this season, rushing for 665 yards and six scores in just five games. Even though the Chiefs have a better record, Seattle is favored at home in this marquee matchup. Let’s take a look at the opening odds and some things to watch for in primetime in Week 7. That then, in turn, puts way too much pressure on this defense. Then there's the Chiefs, a team that has a defense under Steve Spagnuolo that feels tailor-made to be able to put Darnold into turnover-prone positions in this game. Now, to be sure, the Kansas City passing offense hasn't been operating on all cylinders, so I do wonder what Mike Macdonald will have in store to try and bottle up Kenneth Walker III. At the end of the day, though, there's simply more I trust with the Chiefs right now than with Seahawks, so even on the road, give me KC. Easiest NFL Week 7 pick on the board New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Miami Dolphins vs. New York Jets (-4.5) Don't mistake this for having any type of unwavering faith in the New York Jets. It's wavering quite a bit. At the same time, maybe the thing that I'm most confident in right now is the fact that the Miami Dolphins are the worst team in the NFL. Yes, they might win a game randomly at some point this season, but I have a hard time believing that win comes on the road and that it comes against a team that is at least as healthy as the Jets are right now in this moment. The Dolphins don't have anyone that can cover Garrett Wilson or even Omar Cooper Jr. in the passing game, which should give Geno Smith some consistent options in the pass game, while Braelon Allen and the offensive line are getting the run game clicking. The defense is fine overall, but the pass rush against a team that's not without De'Von Achane leads me to believe that Malik Willis is going to have a tough time on Sunday. This feels almost too simple, but I can't pass it up. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) Denver Broncos vs. Arizona Cardinals (+4.5) I know, I know, I know. My Bo Nix slander has gone entirely too far. I can hear you complaining about it now, and it's a fair point, because even after beating the Rams, I'm under no guise that the Cardinals are a high-quality football team. At the same time, though, Nix is playing like the worst quarterback in the NFL right now. Even as someone low on Nix, I didn't expect this type of dramatic dropoff with no real signs of things getting any better. The Cardinals defense is certainly a generous unit, but I don't know if Sean Payton or Nix himself have enough faith in the quarterback right now to fully take advantage of that. Moreover, the defense has, on the whole, been lesser than a year ago and has been quite banged up. While the ceiling of the Cardinals is low, I don't think that Jacoby Brissett is going to make the same back-breaking mistakes we saw Sam Darnold make on Thursday Night Football last week. This feels like a game that could end up being similarly weird to Arizona's win over the Rams this past week, and I'm not only taking the Cards against the spread in this matchup, but give me them to pull off the upset fully while playing at home. home.blurb: Among those practicing fully on Wednesday was receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who was listed as limited the previous two days because of an ankle injury. Smith-Njigba, who leads the NFL in receiving yards and receiving touchdowns, does not have a game status on the final injury report, meaning he is good to go. Also without a status, despite being listed as limited all week with an ankle injury, is defensive lineman Leonard Williams, who played last week through the injury he suffered in a Week 4 win over the Chargers. Also ruled out are linebacker Chazz Surratt, who will miss a third straight game with a calf injury, and running back Zach Charbonnet, who remains on the physically unable to perform list as he works his way back from the torn ACL he suffered in last season's Divisional Round win over the 49ers. For the Broncos, All-Pro cornerback Patrick Surtain II has been ruled out with an ankle injury, as has starting safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle). Starting cornerback Riley Moss, who missed last weekend's game with a rib injury, is questionable after being listed as limited in practice all week. RB Zach Charbonnet (knee, limited participation) CB Riley Moss (ribs, limited participation) Tuesday's injury report, which like Monday's is an estimation of participation, was mostly unchanged from a day earlier. Guard Beau Stephens (shoulder) went from being listed as limited Monday to full participation Tuesday, while every other player's status stayed the same. Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the NFL's leading receiver, was listed as limited for the second straight day due to an ankle injury, as was defensive tackle Leonard Williams. Receiver Irv Charles, who was activated from injured reserve earlier in the day, was again listed as a full participant, another indicator that he is on track to make his Seahawks debut on Thursday. Dallas is off to a slow start at 2-4, and the defense (31st in EPA/Play) remains one of the worst in the NFL. Dak Prescott and Co. have lost back-to-back primetime games against Tampa Bay (Week 5) and Green Bay (Week 6), looking pretty rough in both appearances. So, can they turn things around on the road against a divisional opponent? The Eagles enter this game on a four-game losing streak, and star quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots in his lungs. That is a massive blow to the Eagles in the futures market, as they’re now last in the odds to win the NFC East and +15000 to win the Super Bowl. Tanner McKee is set to make another start in Week 7, and this may turn into a lost season for an Eagles team that could decide to trade some veteran pieces to recoup draft capital and lighten the load on the salary cap in years to come. Oddsmakers have set the Cowboys as favorites in this matchup, and a win would put Dallas in a much better position to win the NFC East – which it is still favored to do. picks.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys were figured to be the two frontrunners in the NFC East this season, with some even considering the duo as Super Bowl contenders. Just six weeks into the season, both teams are closer to booking vacations than they are preparing for a February trip to Los Angeles. Injuries did a number on the Eagles, claiming Saquon Barkley and many more. Recently, Jalen Hurts was added to that list. The quarterback is done for the year with blood clots . As for Dallas, it's still the defense. And it always has been. In recent weeks, though, the Cowboys offense has become a major problem as well. That isn't a winning combination for Brian Schottenheimer, who has seen his job security come into question lately. Both teams are desperate for a win, but at least the Eagles have a built-in excuse. The NFC East is a running joke at this point as in Weeks 5-6, it became the first division since the 1970 AFL-NFL merger to go winless across back-to-week weeks in which all four teams played. So that mediocrity is the only thing saving the Cowboys and Eagles right now. But Philadelphia has lost starting QB Jalen Hurts for the season after doctors out of nowhere discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs. He was initially diagnosed with what was described as a superficial blood clot in his calf that kept him out of Week 5. So, the Eagles might be active ahead of the coming trade deadline with things going so south. Hurts is expected to make a full recovery for next season. He hasn't missed more than two games in a campaign since becoming Philadelphia's starter in 2021. This marks the first of two meetings between the NFC East rivals, with the Eagles in Texas on the American Thanksgiving. They split two meetings last season, each winning at home. It was the first time he averaged fewer than 5 yards per attempt and had multiple picks since Week 3 of the 2018 season. Dallas abandoned the running game and has now dropped five straight primetime matchups. The 2-4 start is the team's worst since 2020. Pro Bowl returner KaVontae Turpin injured his rib on the opening kickoff and was unable to return. Backup QB Tanner McKee got his first start of the season Sunday, and it didn't go very well in a 25-14 home loss to Carolina. The 26-year-old was OK in completing 26 of 45 for 215 yards with a TD, but Philly had only 222 total yards and zero running game without injured running back Saquon Barkley – too early to know if he will play this week. McKee is now 1-2 as a starter in the league and presumably is the guy the rest of the way unless the Eagles add via trade or free agency. The team also has fifth-round rookie Cole Payton out of North Dakota State. Philadelphia's four-game losing streak is the team's longest since 2020, and it hasn't dropped five in a row since 2016. The Eagles have three straight games averaging under 4.0 yards per play, their worst such run since 1999. away.blurb: Dee Winters suffered what was labeled an ankle injury in the first half of the Week 6 loss to the Green Bay Packers and the veteran wasn't able to return after that. Winters wasn't the only notable player to get hurt, as wideout and returner KaVontae Turpin came down with a ribs injury on the opening kickoff and did not return, either. The Cowboys replaced Turpin with wide receiver Jonathan Mingo on punt returns and running back Tyler Goodson on kickoffs. The former averaged six yards per return and had a long of 16 yards and the latter broke off a 30-yard return and averaged 24.4 pre return over five attempts. Putting that aside for now, Overshown finally returned to practice last week and turned in two limited sessions in total, so it appears he's at least getting closer to returning. That said, we have expected Overshown back for a few weeks now, yet the veteran is still out, so nobody should get their hopes up for Overshown returning to the field this week. away.blurb: Cowboys Injury Report: 2 Out, 4 Questionable vs. Packers Home FRISCO, Texas — The Dallas Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant and offensive tackle Drew Shelton for Sunday night’s game at the Green Bay Packers , and listed linebacker DeMarvion Overshown , cornerback Joey Porter Jr. , defensive tackle L.T. Overton , and cornerback Ameer Speed as questionable on Friday’s final injury report. Durant and Shelton did not practice all week with hamstring injuries. Overshown was limited Thursday and Friday with his hamstring after missing Wednesday, and coach Brian Schottenheimer said Friday that he still considers Overshown a long shot. “Yeah, doing okay. Again, I still think it’s probably a long shot for this game, but it was good to see him out there moving around a little bit better,” Schottenheimer said. Porter appeared on the report with an ankle injury. He was limited Wednesday, a full participant Thursday, and limited again Friday. Porter missed last week’s loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers with an illness, and defensive coordinator Christian Parker said Thursday that Porter’s workload would be heavily increased this week. Overton was added to the report Friday with a foot injury and did not practice. Speed was limited Thursday and Friday with a knee injury after missing Wednesday. Packers Rule Out Four, Including Javon Hargrave Green Bay ruled out defensive tackles Jonathan Ford and Javon Hargrave , receiver Skyy Moore , and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste . Defensive tackle Jordon Riley , who is in his 21-day return-to-practice window, is doubtful with an Achilles injury. Guard Aaron Banks is questionable with a knee and toe injury, along with defensive tackle Anthony Campbell with an ankle injury, cornerback Brandon Cisse with a hip injury added Friday, center/guard Jacob Monk with a quadriceps injury, and receiver Savion Williams , who has an ankle injury and is also in his return window. ‘I Just Kept Throwing Up’: Joey Porter Jr. Details Illness That Kept Him Out Against Buccaneers, Targets Green Bay A New Ankle Listing For Joey Porter Jr. Full Go For CeeDee Lamb, Tyler Smith, And Alijah Clark Safety Alijah Clark , who has been dealing with a hamstring injury, practiced fully all three days and carries no game status. away.blurb: LG Aaron Banks (toe/knee): He practiced in a limited capacity all week, but it's his first week back from a multi-week injury. More than likely, the Packers will go with Laken Tomlinson at left guard against the Cowboys. Eventually, the Packers will have to make a long-term decision on their preferred starter at the position. DL Anthony Campbell (ankle) : His likely return from an ankle injury is coming at a good time considering the injury situation along the defensive front. It's possible Campbell will need to play double-digit snaps behind Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks and Chris McClellan on Sunday night. CB Brandon Cisse (hip): An unexpected addition to the injury report. Cisse injured his hip and was limited on Friday, creating the dreaded late-week injury and potential need to scramble for answers at a key position. Carrington Valentine would likely start if Cisse can't go. Depth at cornerback is under real stress ahead of matchup with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. WR Savion Williams (ankle): Is the second-year receiver ready to return from an ankle injury that had him on injured reserve to start the season? A natural replacement option for Skyy Moore, who is out, Williams could provide help as a gadget weapon on offense and in the return game if the Packers activate him to the 53-man roster before Sunday night. WR/KR Skyy Moore (ankle): The Packers' primary kick and punt returner injured his ankle last week and wasn't able to practice this week. It's possible the Packers will activate Savion Williams to help make up for Moore's absence in the return game and at receiver. The Cowboys ruled out cornerback Cobie Durant and rookie offensive lineman Drew Shelton and listed linebacker DeMarvion Overshown, defensive lineman L.T Overton, cornerback Joey Porter Jr. and cornerback Ameer Speed as questionable on the final injury report. DL Jordon Riley (Achilles): He only just returned to practice this week, and even though the Packers need help along the defensive line, Riley is unlikely to play Sunday. He could be a factor as a run stuffer come next week or Week 8. DL Jonathan Ford (calf): His injury, combined with the season-ending injury to Javon Hargrave, puts the Packers in a tough place along the defensive front. Ford likely would have played a lot of snaps on Sunday if healthy. home.headline: Eagles steal QB from Cowboys: Joe Milton expected to sign with Philadelphia after injury to Jalen Hurts
home.blurb: User Menu Settings Log Out Log In Sign Up Fantasy & Games See All ArrowForward # # LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Imagn Images With Jalen Hurts out this week due to a blood clot , the Philadelphia Eagles ended up stealing a player from the Dallas Cowboys . The Eagles are going to sign Joe Milton off of the Cowboys' practice squad, according to multiple reports . Under NFL rules, if you sign a player off another team's practice squad, that player has to be placed on your 53-man roster, so Milton won't be a practice squad player in Philadelphia; he'll be on the actual roster. With the addition of Milton, that means the Eagles will have three quarterbacks heading into Sunday's game against Carolina. Milton will join Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton . Hurts has already been ruled out due to a blood clot in his calf and it's unknown when he can return to the field. For Sunday, the Eagles will hand the starting job over to McKee , but clearly, they weren't comfortable with only having a rookie behind him, which is why they went out and added Milton. There was some speculation that the Eagles might look to bring Andy Dalton back to Philadelphia, but in the end, the team decided to go with Milton. During the 2026 offseason, the Cowboys made a trade for Sam Howell , and he ended up beating Milton out for the backup QB job. The Cowboys ended up cutting Milton after the preseason in a move that seemed to blindside the 26-year-old QB. The fact that the Eagles are adding a quarterback likely signifies that Hurts will be out for more than one game. If they thought he was only going to be out for a week, they probably would have been comfortable with Payton as the backup for just one game, but if Hurts is going to miss an extended amount of time, then it certainly makes sense to add another quarterback, which is what Philly ended up doing. The Eagles didn't go into detail about the nature of the clot that Hurts is dealing with, but ESPN has reported that he'll be out indefinitely "until this situation is solved." At this point, it seems like almost a given that the Eagles will end up putting Hurts on injured reserve. If they DON'T go that route, that means they'd have to carry four quarterbacks on their 53-man roster, which wouldn't make sense for a team that currently has 24 players on its injury report.
